title: Central Bureau of Investigation v. Bholu (Ryan International School Murder)
crime_type: School Premise Stabbing / Premeditated Minor Homicide to Postpone Exams
court_or_authority: Special Children Court Gurugram / High Court of Punjab & Haryana / Supreme Court of India
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 15 Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015
evidence: CCTV camera footage showing accused entering school ground-floor washroom shortly before victim child entered and exiting hurriedly
Serrated hunting knife recovered from commode reservoir following suspect disclosure statement
Forensic blood DNA analysis connecting knife blade residue to deceased 7-year-old victim Prince
CBI digital extraction of internet history searching how to commit murder and postpone parent-teacher meetings
modus_operandi: Senior high school student desperate to defer scheduled parent-teacher meetings and upcoming semester examinations brought a concealed kitchen knife to school. Waited inside the elementary school washroom for a solitary victim, slit the throat of an innocent 7-year-old boy, dumped weapon in the water tank, and informed staff to trigger emergency evacuation.
personality_disorder: Severe academic stress maladaptation, pathological egocentrism, and psychopathic lack of victim empathy.
common_traits: Concealment of edged weapon inside educational institution
Killing random vulnerable younger student to cause institutional shutdown
Attempted framing of school bus conductor during initial local police probe
Pre-crime digital search on evading exams via violent disruption
summary: Landmark Supreme Court jurisprudence on preliminary assessment under Section 15 of Juvenile Justice Act 2015, ruling that an accused aged 16-18 accused of a heinous crime can be tried as an adult based on mental and physical capacity evaluation.
